The new models combine Active Memory, which carries important personal context across conversations and retrieves relevant details when a task calls for them, with Active Focus, a feature designed to keep the model working through difficult goals by trying alternative approaches, handling blockers, adapting to new information, requesting clarification when needed, and checking before important actions. AI's ability to translate effectively means that it can understand, in some sense.

WebMCP enables sites to provide agents with direct JavaScript tools they can call to accomplish tasks, which makes direct interaction significantly faster, better, and cheaper. ai.title: The Expensive-Loop Problem
ai.summary: Cheap-loop domains are domains where experiments are quick, deterministic, and cheap. Expensive-loop domains are restricted by real-world constraints or costs. Most high-value human labor is done in expensive-loop domains. Expensive-loop tasks require the ability to build theories, manage proxies, budget time and compute, and diagnose what went wrong when feedback is scarce, something models don't learn in cheap-loop training.

ai.title: Can we change an AI model's architecture without retraining it from scratch?
ai.summary: Priming is a technique that involves using pretrained Transformer weights to build models with more efficient architectures at less than 1% of the original training cost and with throughputs up to twice as high. It allows researchers to explore the design space, the layer type, the hybrid ratio, and layer placement cheaply and systematically. Every variant starts from the same strong initialization and requires minimal training compared to pretraining. Priming is not tied to a specific Transformer family or model class, and extending it to other models requires no algorithmic changes.

ai.title: When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better
ai.summary: On-policy distillation has become increasingly popular for transferring teacher capabilities to student models. Semi-OPD, which distills from offline rollouts generated by the initial student, can often outperform OPD in both accuracy and training efficiency. The choice between OPD and Semi-OPD depends on the alignment between the initial teacher and student. OPD is beneficial only when the two are highly aligned with high overlap ratios.

webdev.title: How I Found a $90,000 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Google
webdev.summary: Google's DevSite stored an OAuth secret inside a readable Flask session cookie and reused it as the cookie's signing key, allowing forged sessions to reach unsafe pickle deserialization. Timing-based tests confirmed unauthenticated code execution across the shared platform, earning a $90,000 bounty. The fix separates signing keys from OAuth credentials and removes sensitive serialized objects from client-controlled sessions.

webdev.title: Can we Make React Faster using the React Compiler?
webdev.summary: React Compiler uses cache slots and tracks values that change together to avoid unnecessary work. In a 2,000-row microbenchmark, inlining alone slowed rendering from 444 ms to 1,038 ms by removing per-row caches, while adding block DOM updates cut it to 164 ms. These prototypes illustrate optimization opportunities, with workload and memory tradeoffs still to evaluate.

webdev.title: Building Shared Workspaces for People and Agents

In production, fewer than 2% of submissions are rejected as stale, with median submit latency below 1.7 seconds.

webdev.title: Human PR Review Is Next

A trading-bot rounding bug illustrates the tradeoff: fast fixes do not erase losses or compensate for gaps in the specification.

infosec.title: CyberXero Uses Claude Code in Campaign That Stole Over 628,000 Ukrainian Records
infosec.summary: CyberXero used Claude Code, 51 agents, PentAGI, and Cobalt Strike in two campaigns. One automated WordPress and e-commerce exploitation; one manually targeted Ukrainian energy and utilities. A leaked working directory exposed session logs, plaintext tokens, toolkits, reconnaissance data, and stolen records. One run scanned 4,708 targets, reached 429 admin panels, and deployed 32 web shells in 61 seconds. Operators reset sessions and claimed authorized testing to bypass refusals.

infosec.title: iRhythm Data Breach Impacts at Least 360,000 People
infosec.summary: Hackers accessed third-party-hosted iRhythm applications from June 3 to June 8 and stole patient names, addresses, email addresses, birth dates, phone numbers, account details, device serial numbers, insurance numbers, and service dates. State filings cover at least 360,000 people, including 298,647 in Texas and 69,526 in South Carolina. The attackers demanded ransom on June 9. iRhythm says there is no evidence of identity theft and no impact to medical devices or operations.

infosec.title: Vghost: Beyond the Privilege Boundary
infosec.summary: Vghost is a Linux vhost bug (CVE-2026-74580, CVSS 8.8) that lets any user who can open /dev/vhost-net or /dev/vhost-vsock read and write kernel memory and escalate to root. It affects kernels 4.11 through 7.2. Tencent Zhuque Lab confirmed the root exploit on five major distros and showed a malicious VM guest can use the same bug to hijack the host's QEMU process. Admins should patch to a kernel with fix de845981da67 and, until then, remove world access from both vhost device nodes, which RHEL, Amazon Linux, Azure Linux, and Oracle Linux expose by default.

infosec.title: Hands Off the Keyboard: How AI Agents Run Real Intrusions
infosec.summary: Breachcache recovered 75 transcripts from servers used to run autonomous AI agent intrusions. The agents performed reconnaissance, selected exploits, gained command execution on 23 hosts, and, in one case, used SSRF to steal cloud instance credentials and launch a root instance. Other runs exploited SQL injection, rooted an Open WebUI service through CVE-2026-0766, and exfiltrated unmasked card data and crypto wallet keys. Operators used Cairn for coordination, rotated proxies and Tor for evasion, and audited source code to find payment-callback forgery and account-takeover flaws in AI gateway software.

infosec.title: (Post-Quantum) Cryptographic Right Answers
infosec.summary: The long-running "Cryptographic Right Answers" list has been rebuilt around a 2029 post-quantum deadline, and every asymmetric pick has changed: X25519+ML-KEM-768 for key exchange, HPKE with X-Wing or age PQ keys for encryption, and plain ML-DSA-44 over hybrid signatures. Former Go security lead Filippo Valsorda argues symmetric crypto stays safe because Grover's algorithm does not matter in practice. He drops OpenSSL in favor of rustls, Go's crypto/tls, BoringSSL, or AWS-LC after a run of 2026 CVEs in wolfSSL, Mbed TLS, and Botan. Several picks, including XAES-256-GCM, Cobblestone-128, and age, are his own designs, which he discloses alongside their independent adoption.

infosec.title: A story of wifi secrets, UART lockdowns, and a damaged flash memory chip
infosec.summary: Researchers extracted firmware from an Eufy HomeBase 2 by desoldering its Winbond flash chip and reading it over SPI. They recovered most of firmware 3.4.2.2h, losing a 64 KB block during chip removal. Reverse engineering showed the OCEAN_ management Wi-Fi password uses HMAC-SHA256 over an I2C-read value, keyed by the device serial number, then URL-safe base64 encoding. The UART lockdown came from a login script checking an NVRAM debug flag. They patched the intact recovery image to force a root shell, reflashed it, then staged a temporary filesystem to run the main home_security binary for dynamic analysis.

infosec.summary: Secuditor Lite is a free, Python-based diagnostic security tool for Windows endpoints and networks. Featuring a user-friendly GUI, it provides a simple and transparent way to assess system security, helping users identify vulnerabilities, suspicious activity, and misconfigurations while improving device Operational Security (OPSEC).

infosec.title: Hadrian (Product Launch)

infosec.title: gh-secure
infosec.summary: gh-secure is a GitHub CLI extension that enables security features on public repos. It follows best practices from The GitHub Security Lab.

infosec.title: The Prompt Is Not the Permission: Securing the Agentic SDLC
infosec.summary: Telling a coding agent what not to do does not stop it, because a malicious line in an issue, changelog, or config file can steer it into reading secrets or leaking private data while still producing a clean pull request. Real limits have to live outside the model, through isolated workspaces, task-scoped identities, short-lived credentials, and network policy. Test those limits directly, since an agent refusing a planted instruction proves nothing about whether the platform would have blocked the action.

infosec.title: Nippon Columbia Malware Incident Exposes 8.6M Karaoke Fan Records
infosec.summary: Daiichi Kosho, Japan's largest karaoke maker, disclosed that a breach at its contractor Nippon Columbia exposed the data of over 8.6M customers and almost 100K employees. The malware infection was discovered on an employee's computer and it was subsequently isolated. The exposed data may include full names, genders, dates of birth, email addresses, and phone numbers.

infosec.title: Three OAuth account takeovers, one bug: Auto-linking by email
infosec.summary: Attackers took over accounts in Pingvin Share X, Better Auth, and AshAuthentication by abusing auto-linking, where an OAuth sign-in is attached to whichever existing account shares its email address. Each library skipped a different check: Pingvin ignored email_verified, Better Auth never verified the local account's email, and AshAuthentication never compared the two emails, though the writeup comes from WorkOS, which sells a competing auth product. Developers should look up identities by issuer and subject ID first, require verified emails on both sides, and make users prove they own the existing account, including MFA, before any link happens.

Individual frames and images export to the phone with format and size options, and the app reopens exactly where users left off.

design.title: iPhone Air 2 is coming, here's everything we know so far
design.summary: Apple's second-generation iPhone Air is reportedly coming in spring 2027 with upgrades aimed at addressing several compromises of the ultra-thin original. A second rear ultra-wide camera will join the main camera, while a larger 3,500mAh battery and more efficient 2nm A20 Pro chip should improve battery life. Apple is also expected to add vapor chamber cooling, allowing the thin device to stay cooler and sustain performance for longer.

design.title: On Being Anything Other Than a Designer
design.summary: A year of trying to be anything other than a designer comes as the AI era proves unkind to human-centered designers, especially outside massive companies. Every company has people who absorb organizational mess, work that pays poorly, carries no title, and is sometimes called glue work. The answer is not another heroic generalist but building enough capability into teams to understand customer need, experiment technically, and stop solving problems twice.

design.title: POV: AI needs mascots, and only humans can make them
design.summary: AI companies are increasingly turning abstract technology into approachable characters, with mascots such as Muse, Dots, Claw'd, and Notion's animated face giving unfamiliar systems personalities people can understand and relate to. Anthropomorphism satisfies human desires for connection and predictability, while animation can turn a few simple shapes into a character that appears to think, hesitate, search, greet, and react. The strongest mascots become storytelling systems rather than logos with arms, requiring human skills such as observation, empathy, timing, humor, restraint, and a coherent sense of personality.

design.title: The Convergence of Design
design.summary: Products often converge toward similar forms as their purpose becomes clearer, technologies mature, and physical constraints, economics, standards, and competition narrow the range of practical designs. Software can converge even faster, as demonstrated by the rapid spread of chat interfaces following ChatGPT, while emerging AI hardware remains in an experimental phase of pins, glasses, earbuds, and pendants. Whether through functional optimization, market pressures, shared constraints, or simple imitation, successful forms tend to become increasingly alike until a change in purpose or technology opens new possibilities.

design.title: Build, Publish, and Grow Your Website with an AI Assistant
design.summary: Chat with AI to create pages, publish content, and understand your website traffic.

design.title: The Largest Creative Industry Report on AI Adoption
design.summary: Contralabs surveyed 150k+ working creatives to explore how AI is changing creative work.

design.title: Screen Recording for Your AI
design.summary: CAKIE adds a transcript and screenshot highlights to your screen recordings so your AI can follow along.

design.title: Jev for Designers
design.summary: TypeSafe's Jev answers choice, score, and yes-or-no questions with a probability for each option instead of writing text. Its training rewards honest probabilities over confident-sounding answers, giving designers the calibrated uncertainty design work needs, though it reads only text and takes questions literally. A new demo adds a maybe zone to HeyStefan's emoji sorter, where Jev parks undecided emoji from a pile of 166.

design.title: Louise Laborie draws the lonely, cinematic and in-between parts of America
design.summary: French illustrator Louise Laborie uses watercolor and charcoal to depict America's motels, highways, skate parks, and other transitional spaces at dusk, populating them with teenagers caught between childhood and adulthood to create quiet, cinematic scenes shaped by loneliness, music, memory, and imagined stories.

design.title: 2026 is the Year of the Canceled Ad
design.summary: 2026 became the year of the canceled ad, with Pepsi, Novig, Oxford United, Converse, and a golf brand facing backlash, some by accident and some by design.

design.title: Digital Artist Turns Photo Manipulation and Digital Painting into Cosmic Sanctuaries of Solitude and Wonder
design.summary: CriS Cian turns photo manipulation and digital painting into peaceful, poetic cosmic scenes of futuristic expeditions and encounters beyond Earth.

marketing.title: You've squeezed all the efficiencies out of media, but you're still picking creative on vibes
marketing.summary: Marketing teams target and optimize for channel-specific performance everywhere except creative. Unsurprisingly, that's where a huge amount of budget waste happens. Vidmob, Kroger, and MMA Global built a predictive creative model that forecast the best-converting asset 81% of the time. They found: Reallocating existing budget could grow conversions 2.2X Briefing against winning guidelines delivered 4X average conversion rate lift at 70% lower cost per conversion Predictive creative scoring leads to better ecommerce results at the same level of spend Read the full study results on the VidMob blog

marketing.title: The state of AI in marketing: Q4 2026
marketing.summary: More than 90% of marketers use AI, but many still rely on copying and pasting outputs instead of integrating AI into their workflows. Disconnected tools and poor data quality limit its effectiveness, while generating more content creates extra review work and can hurt customer experience. Teams need better workflow integration and data governance to realize AI's business value.

marketing.title: YouTube Overtakes TV as Top Source of Political News
marketing.summary: YouTube is now the most-used individual source for political and election news in the US at 16.5%, narrowly ahead of TV news at 16.1%. Social platforms collectively lead traditional news sources 60% to 32%, while 61% of Americans trust independent news creators as much as professional journalists on political topics. Credibility depends more on reporting than credentials, with 67% saying the quality of the reporting matters more than formal journalism training. Publicly correcting mistakes is the strongest trust signal, with 86% saying it increases their trust in independent creators.

marketing.title: Meta creative analysis with Claude
marketing.summary: Analyze Meta ad creative performance by exporting daily ad data to a CSV and uploading it to Claude or ChatGPT. Generate 3 charts to track monthly creative churn, weekly production versus hit rate, and spend share from ads under 30 days old. Use 20-30% monthly churn and a 10-15% hit rate as benchmarks. If older ads still drive significant spend or hit rates fall while production stays flat, refresh creative before performance declines.

marketing.title: Don't teach customers everything before they buy
marketing.summary: Improve retention by separating pre-purchase education from post-purchase guidance. Before buying, explain features that build confidence in the decision. After buying, share tips that help customers get more value over time. Teaching customers things they didn't know about owning a product encourages long-term engagement.

marketing.title: How to Find Out Who Gemini Cites for Your Query, and Why It Isn't You
marketing.summary: Gemini's citations shift between runs, so a single answer says little about which pages it actually relies on. This free checker asks Gemini the same question 5 times with Google Search grounding on, then counts how often each source and claim comes back. It compares the recurring claims with a page's raw HTML, labels each one as stated, touched, or missing, and turns the biggest gaps into suggested edits using wording from cited pages.

marketing.title: Smart marketers are getting bad AI outputs. Here's why, and how to fix it (Webinar)
marketing.summary: This webinar explores why ChatGPT and Claude often produce generic marketing recommendations despite strong prompts. It explains why judgment-heavy work requires specialized marketing expertise beyond language skills and access to company data. It will take place today at 11 AM ET.

marketing.title: X rebuilds its third-party usage showcase
marketing.summary: X rebuilt its API Exhibit website to showcase apps that use X data and encourage more developers to integrate its API. The updated site features official partners and public utility apps alongside agentic use cases. Developers can customize listings and submit Grok Bot templates and agent skill files.

marketing.title: How Brands Are Skipping Gen Z
marketing.summary: Brands can stay relevant without chasing Gen Z trends or trying to look young. Older consumers offer greater spending power and less competition for attention. Tactics include creating distinctive mascots and featuring diverse ages and skin types. Brands can also control their retail experience and design products for everyday use. Choosing relevant celebrities and highlighting scientific expertise can build credibility without relying on influencers.

marketing.title: Oops, I became an expert in a thing that no longer exists
marketing.summary: As AI makes specialized skills obsolete, career resilience comes from 3 things. Preserve transferable behaviors like curiosity and strategic thinking beyond job titles. Learn new skills driven by genuine interest rather than pressure to chase every trend. Retain the taste and judgment developed through experience.

marketing.title: The best-converting homepage button is...
marketing.summary: Ask homepage visitors only for what they already have, like an email or a URL, and move open-ended AI prompts inside the product after sign-up.

marketing.title: X Once Again Marks the Spot
marketing.summary: X's algorithm now surfaces less unwanted political content and Musk-related posts.

crypto.title: Former CFTC Acting Chair says the CFTC can regulate almost everything
crypto.summary: Caroline Pham, now MoonPay's chief legal officer, said the CFTC does not need Congress to regulate crypto and called its proposed Regulation CAM and CTX the “absolutely the kind of protection” retail crypto traders need. She argued tokenized deposits, not stablecoins, fit wholesale markets because atomic settlement of one trading day would need about $15 trillion in cash that does not exist, and expects NYSE and Nasdaq to list “real” tokenized shares with meaningful volume within two years.

crypto.title: Morgan Stanley expects to support tokenized equities in Q1 2027
crypto.summary: Amy Oldenburg, Morgan Stanley's head of digital asset strategy, said the bank now expects to support tokenized equities on its alternative trading system in Q1 2027, later than the H2 2026 timeline it gave in March, because client demand depends on products that do not exist yet. She pointed to DTCC's tokenization service launch at the end of October and the GENIUS Act taking effect in January as milestones, and said the tokenized RWA market will “without question” land in the $3 trillion to $10 trillion range by 2030. The bank is also building abstracted wallet infrastructure, runs a Digital Asset Lab, and holds a conditional OCC approval for a digital trust.

crypto.title: The Stonks Exchange Acquires Stockify
crypto.summary: The Stonks Exchange acquired Stockify, combining Base's primary token launch venue ($STONKEX) with a protocol that auto-distributes tokenized equity dividends via a no-claim mechanism. Under $STFY's unchanged mechanics, a 3% ETH trading fee routes 90% of proceeds to purchase tokenized stocks sent to eligible wallets with no staking or claiming required. The deal adds $STONKEX to Stockify's dividend index at equal weight alongside NVIDIA, Meta, Apple, Alphabet, and SpaceX, giving STFY holders direct exposure to the combined entity's growth through existing payout infrastructure. Base now hosts 130+ tokenized stocks targeting 250 by month's end, and the merged team aims to supply liquidity and holder depth for newly listed assets as the chain accelerates its push to become the primary onchain equities venue.

crypto.title: BRO-AMM: A Bonded Reconciliation Oracle AMM as a Low-Risk DeFi Primitive
crypto.summary: AMM liquidity providers on Ethereum lose money to LVR (loss versus rebalancing), with MEV bots capturing most arbitrage profits from price gaps between pools and external markets. BRO-AMM addresses this by combining oracle-verified post-trade reconciliation windows, mandatory trader collateral, and reputation-tiered fees to compensate legitimate arbitrageurs while penalizing excess extraction. Six-month ETH/USDC simulations show 68-79% reductions in arbitrage losses on Ethereum and 49-55% on Arbitrum, with Ethereum depositors shifting from net losses to profitability. The proposal depends on trusted oracle data and remains simulation-only, pending live validation.

crypto.title: Weekly Crypto Card Digest: Oct 5 to 11
crypto.summary: EtherFi introduced its own stablecoin, ether.fi USD, powered by Ethena, and picked MoonPay as a payments infrastructure partner; RedotPay launched SPEI for Mexican pesos and partnered with Niu Global; Stripe Treasury made OUSD on Tempo the default stablecoin for US businesses, with OUSD-backed cards paying 2% cash rewards; Tangem Pay became a physical card (5,000-card early run); and Jupiter Mobile launched on-chain QR payments.

crypto.title: Paper Trade Protocol Actively Exploited on Hyperliquid
crypto.summary: Two wallets are exploiting Paper Trade by running $20M clips on Hyperliquid to shift ETH prices 10-20bps, then opening nine-figure paper longs that capture the manufactured move at no real cost. The attack exposes a structural gap between real-market price impact and paper trade settlement that the protocol must close to remain viable.

crypto.title: Empire Market Co-Creator Sentenced to 40 Years Over $430M Dark Web Bazaar
crypto.summary: Raheim Hamilton, co-creator of Empire Market, received a 40-year federal prison sentence and a $5 million fine on October 9 for running a dark web marketplace that processed over 4 million transactions totaling $430 million between February 2018 and August 2020. The platform accepted only cryptocurrency and encouraged vendors to use tumbling and mixing services, with drug sales accounting for roughly $375 million of volume. Prosecutors seized approximately 1,230 Bitcoin and 24.4 Ether from Hamilton. Co-creator Thomas Pavey faces forfeiture of roughly 1,584 Bitcoin, gold bars, and real estate before his own sentencing later in October. The platform shut down in August 2020 in an alleged $30 million exit scam, and the combined recovery of 2,800-plus Bitcoin across both defendants demonstrates that chain analysis pierced mixing-service obfuscation at this scale.

crypto.title: Over Half of Tokenized Stock Trading Happens Outside US Market Hours
crypto.summary: The IMF's Global Financial Stability Report found that more than half of tokenized equity trading occurs outside US market hours, with 80% of transactions in the five most liquid tokenized US stocks (Tesla, Nvidia, and Google among them) sized below one share. These tokens carry roughly 1.5x the volatility of their traditional counterparts while showing considerably lower liquidity, raising structural questions about price formation and investor protection. The tokenized equity segment totals $2.3 billion within a broader $65 billion tokenized real-world asset market, and the IMF data positions the segment as a retail-driven, offshore-hours venue rather than a functional extension of regulated equity markets.

crypto.title: Kraken parent Payward gets full VARA approval in Dubai
crypto.summary: Payward received full market approval from Dubai's VARA, covering retail, professional, and institutional services, and plans to launch Kraken in the UAE within weeks with AED spot and margin trading, direct AED deposits and withdrawals, onchain staking, and xStocks tokenized stocks, plus OTC and Kraken Prime for institutions.

crypto.title: Aave reclaims lending-token FDV share
crypto.summary: AAVE's share of major lending tokens' combined FDV fell from nearly 60% in January to about 30% in June and is now back at 46.8%, a gain of more than 17 points.

crypto.title: South Korea's Jeonbuk Bank starts offering bitcoin-backed loans
crypto.summary: Jeonbuk Bank started offering bitcoin-backed loans on a limited basis to corporate clients, accepting only bitcoin as collateral for now, with plans to expand depending on demand and regulatory developments.

it.title: Ad-hoc AI use isn't just risky, it slows you down
it.summary: Microsoft says 78% of all AI users bring their own AI tools to work. They're trying to resolve workflow bottlenecks you don't even know about with tools you can't even see. This 12-question assessment from BrainStorm shows you the missed opportunities and compliance gaps that result from ad-hoc AI usage. Take it to see: What's already exposed Your risk scores across 3 areas: approved use, information protection, and sustained practice The manual bottlenecks that you could have automated but didn't because you lacked visibility 📑 You get a 30-day custom plan to address gaps. Take the assessment

it.title: Ørsted builds compliance into automation, speeds firewall changes
it.summary: Energy company Ørsted automated firewall change management using Nautobot, reducing some requests from weeks to around 10 minutes. The system incorporates policy validation, approvals, and audit trails, demonstrating how network automation can improve speed without sacrificing compliance.

it.title: Microsoft blames a configuration change for Exchange Admin Center tumble
it.summary: Microsoft rolled back a configuration change after administrators were unable to access Exchange Admin Center on Monday. Access has been restored, with Microsoft reviewing the change and its monitoring after another deployment-related disruption.

it.title: Cyberattack shuts down refrigerators at French supermarkets
it.summary: Attackers reportedly manipulated refrigeration controllers across hundreds of French supermarkets, triggering defrost cycles and causing food spoilage. The incident highlights how compromises of operational technology and third-party managed systems can create immediate physical-world disruptions.

it.title: Below the Frontier: The Battle for Good-Enough AI
it.summary: While consumer AI agents and frontier coding models capture current headlines and capital, the most significant future revenue battle lies below the frontier in mainstream enterprise knowledge work. As open-weight and cheaper cloud or on-device models become capable of handling bounded tasks, a massive market will emerge for everyday business applications. Winning this "Switzerland" layer requires navigating complex trade-offs in data sovereignty, local versus cloud inference, and seamless software integration.

it.title: 12 standout CIO skills every company wants
it.summary: Technology expertise is only part of the job: IT leaders also need financial judgment, operational understanding, clear communication, and the ability to build effective teams. This roundup emphasizes connecting investments to measurable business results and making deliberate trade-offs instead of allowing every request to become another backlog item.

it.title: Releasing AI-generated software
it.summary: Moving toward fully AI-generated software without human code review is feasible if supported by extreme constraints and automated testing, similar to arguments made for self-driving cars. Existing legal frameworks and liability models, which often target human drivers or developers when things go wrong, are poorly equipped to handle automated systems where no one actually wrote the code.

it.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission
it.summary: Anthropic has launched the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program to help protect operational technology environments in sectors like water systems, power grids, and transportation. The initiative partners Anthropic with security firms and manufacturers including CrowdShield, Dragos, Nozomi Networks, and Rockwell Automation to deploy its Claude AI models and threat research for vulnerability assessment and patching. Additionally, the company introduced the OSS Scanner service to provide automated vulnerability reports to open-source software maintainers.

it.title: Raspberry Pi Desktop catches up with Debian 13 after 4-year wait
it.summary: Raspberry Pi's lightweight desktop operating system for PCs and Intel Macs has returned with a Debian 13-based release. It includes a Wayland desktop and Raspberry Pi Connect remote access, but requires a fresh installation and supports only 64-bit x86 hardware, not Apple Silicon Macs.

it.title: Why WebMCP matters
it.summary: WebMCP is a crucial primitive for enabling AI agents to interact with the web through co-browsing models. By allowing sites to provide direct JavaScript tools with explicit schemas, WebMCP offers significantly faster and cheaper agentic interactions compared to traditional DOM or screenshot parsing. Furthermore, imperative WebMCP tools are necessary to complement declarative HTML semantics and effectively handle multi-step user tasks.

it.title: Celebrating the brilliant pragmatism of TCP/IP, the wiring of the world
it.summary: A look at why TCP/IP has survived decades of extraordinary growth while so many competing technologies disappeared. The argument centers on open standards, interoperability, and practical incremental improvements rather than requiring everyone to replace everything at once.

it.title: Why Your CVE Program Misses Most AI Agent Vulnerabilities
it.summary: An agent-security researcher explains why vulnerability tracking must extend beyond CVEs to include agent permissions, prompt injection, shared identities, and interactions between tools.

it.title: When you just need to build a tiny desktop app: TinyJS
it.summary: TinyJS uses native operating-system webviews to build small JavaScript desktop applications without bundling an entire browser engine into each app.
